fields.title: Creating DataFlows in Magic ETL
fields.description:
For times when you need to transform your DataSets before you can make compelling visualizations, you can use Magic ETL DataFlows to transform multiple DataSets into a new DataSet that you can use to power up cards

This app will help you continue to develop your skills using a variety of Magic ETL transforms to create DataFlows.

pages.name: What is Magic ETL and where do I find it?
pages.displayName: What is Magic ETL and where do I find it?

fields.title: What is Magic ETL and where do I find it?
fields.description:
ETL is short for Extract, Transform, Load. This is an important process that allows data from many disparate sources to be put in one place to transform quickly for easier data analysis.

Magic ETL DataFlows let you visually define and sequence operations to transform your Domo DataSets—without learning SQL or leaving Domo.

You can find Magic ETL in the list of options under the Add tool.

pages.name: When you should use Magic ETL
pages.displayName: When you should use Magic ETL

fields.title: When should you use Magic ETL?
fields.description: In order to maximize the value you get from Domo, it's important to know which transformation tools will work best for you given your needs and skill set.
fields.instructions: Select each pinpoint to review at least two of the key reasons Magic ETL might serve as your best option for transforming data in Domo.

pinpoints.copy:
Use Magic ETL when you need to combine your data with other data or perform more detailed analysis of multiple DataSets.

Magic ETL DataFlows allow you to perform the following actions:

  • Standard filtering
  • Value-mapping (CASE statements)
  • Date manipulations
  • Standard joins
  • Union DataSets with different schemas
  • Replace texts
  • Collapse/uncollapse columns
  • Multiple outputs
  • Standard calculations
  • Data-type reassignment
  • Substring string values

Magic ETL is the best choice for you if you’re new to data transformation. Magic ETL offers a visual query builder, is easy to learn and maintain, and can handle large DataSets, in most cases, more efficiently than MySQL.

fields.title: Magic ETL Interface
fields.description: Creating a Magic ETL DataFlow is simple with the intuitive drag-and-drop interface. Drag an input DataSet onto the canvas, then add tiles to specify how the DataSets should be joined and transformed. In Magic ETL DataFlows, your DataSets are extracted and loaded automatically, and transformed based on actions in the Magic ETL DataFlow.
fields.instructions: Let’s get familiar with the ETL interface. Select each button to learn more about what these elements can help you build in your DataFlow. Find even more information about Magic ETL and each individual action in our Knowledge Base.

pinpoints.copy:
When creating ETL Dataflows each DataFlow should:

  • Include descriptive names for each step of the transformation.
  • Include a description of the input DataSets being merged or manipulated and the DataSet being created, and should also indicate the owner of the data.
  • Be named the same as the output DataFlow—this allows for easy identification of which DataSets are produced by which DataFlows.
Run a preview to see how each action tile transforms your data in the DataFlow.
Set your DataFlow to run automatically based on when your input DataSet(s) update. If none are chosen, the DataFlow will need to be run manually.

To start a DataFlow you’ll drag an Input Dataset tile over to the Magic canvas. To complete a DataSet you’ll select the Output DatSet tile. This will create an output DataSet that you can then use to create visualizations from after you’ve completed your data transforms.

Text tiles refer to components used to manipulate and transform text data within your ETL workflows. These functions help clean, format, and standardize textual data as part of your data transformation process in Magic ETL.
These tiles help you perform essential numeric and date transformations in your ETL processes.
The actions in this section provide you with the ability to transform your DataSet by changing each column in a way that provides you with the information you will need in visualizations.
The Edit Data actions allow you to transform your data to meet your specific needs.

There are two methods for combining data in an ETL transformation: the Append Rows action, which lets you stack rows from multiple DataSets into one DataSet; and the Join Data action, which lets you add columns from one dataset to another.

Aggregating allows you to:

  • Group by - Combine data from multiple rows into specified groups.
  • Rank and Window - Use rank and windowe funtions on your data.

The Pivot tile allows you to:

  • Dynamic unpivot - Narrows a table by pivoting all column data, except those specififed, into new rows. Any columns not excluded will become row values.
  • Pivot - Widens a table by pivoting row values into new columns.
  • Unpivot - Narrows a table by pivoting column values into new rows.
These scripting tiles provide powerful ways to extend Magic ETL capabilities using popular programming languages.
These tiles empower you to embed advanced analytics and machine learning directly within your ETL workflows.
These tiles help streamline your data by minimizing unnecessary columns, boosting processing speed and manageability.
These tiles integrate AI-powered capabilities directly into your ETL workflows for smarter data processing and insights.

fields.title: Add Tiles from Canvas
fields.description: Magic ETL now includes the ability to add a tile directly to the canvas. The feature improves the speed of DataFlow creation and overall workflow efficiency.
fields.instructions: Select the button below to learn more.

pinpoints.copy: Just click the little"plus" button that appears next to all non-terminal tiles on the canvas​. A menu allows you to search for the tile you want, or scroll through the list of tiles to choose one, with most commonly used tiles listed at the top.​

fields.title: Magic ETL activity 1
fields.description:
For your first Magic ETL activity in this module, we'll start with a scenario. Let's say your manager has requested that you build a card that will show a comparison of different years of sales data.
 
Complete the tasks below using the Magic Orders 2025, Magic Orders 2026, and Magic Orders 2027 DataSets, found in the course menu before this training.

tasks.label: Task 1:
tasks.copy:
First, it's important to create the DataSets that you will use in the DataFlow.

  1. Download the Magic Orders 2025, 2026, and 2027 DataSets listed in the course syllabus.
  2. In Domo, navigate to Datasets using the left side menu.
  3. Select Upload a spreadsheet in the Connect Data ribbon.
  4. Click browse your files and select the Magic Orders 2025 file or drag and drop the file to the pop-up window.
  5. Make sure the preview looks correct and click Next.
  6. Enter Magic Orders 2025 as the DataSet name.
  7. Click save.
  8. Repeat these steps for both the Magic Orders 2026 and Magic Orders 2027 files.

tasks.label: Task 2:
tasks.copy:
1. Go to Create (+) in the left side menu in Domo and select Transform Data and then Magic ETL to open a new ETL canvas.
  2. In the left menu, under DataSets, click and drag three Input DataSet icons onto the canvas.
  3. Select the first input and assign the Magic Orders 2025 DataSet to it.
  4. Repeat this same step for the next two Input DataSets: Magic Orders 2026 and Magic Orders 2027.

tasks.label: Task 3:
tasks.copy:
1. Expand the Utility section on the left.
  2. Drag one Select Columns tile over for each of the three DataSets and connect them.
  3. Click the Select Columns tile that is connected to the Magic Orders 2025 input.
  4. Select Add All Columns and rename the following columns: OrdDate to "Order Date", ProductCost to "Item Cost", and ProductPrice to "Item Price".
  5. Select Done.
  6. Repeat these steps for the other Select Columns tiles and rename the following columns:
    Magic Orders 2026: OrderDate to "Order Date", Qty to "Quantity", ItemCost to "Item Cost", and ItemPrice to "Item Price".
    Magic Orders 2027: OrderDate to "Order Date", Qty to "Quantity", ItemCost to "Item Cost", and ItemPrice to "Item Price".

tasks.label: Task 4:
tasks.copy:
1. Under Combine Data, drag an Append Rows tile to the canvas.
  2. Connect all three DataSets to the Append Rows tile.
  3. In the first step dropdown option, select Include All Columns and select Done.
  4. Now select the Run Preview button to ensure it's all working correctly.
  5. Select the Preview tab under the Append Rows tile to ensure the data appears as it should, with all the correct column names in place.

tasks.label: Task 5:
tasks.copy:
1. Drag an Output Dataset tile over to the canvas.
  2. Connect it to the Append Rows tile.
  3. Change the Output DataSet name to "Combined Sales Data," adding your initials.
  4. Next, type this same name into the DataFlow name field: "Combined Sales Data" with your initials.
  5. Then, select Save and Run from the orange arrow drop-down next to Save.

Great job. Now you're ready to move on to ETL activity 2: Part 1.

fields.title: Magic ETL Activity 2: Part 1
fields.description:
In this next activity, let's say your manager now wants you to create a DataFlow that will allow you to build cards that answer the business question, “Are we hitting our sales forecast goals?”

Complete the tasks below using the following DataSets: Power User Sales 2026, Power User Sales 2027, Power User Sales 2028, and Power User Forecast.

tasks.label: Task 1:
tasks.copy:
1. Download the Power User Forecast DataSet from the course syllabus as you did before.
  2. Using the file upload connector, create a new DataSet.
  3. Open a new Magic ETL DataFlow.
  4. Add the Power User Forecast DataSet you just created as an input.
  5. Next, under Pivot, drag and drop an Unpivot (Collapse Columns) tile to the canvas.
  6. Connect it to the input tile.

    Note:  In the following transform step, you are turning the 4 product column headers into row values distributed by month and year. Your actual forecast amounts for each product by month and year will be its own column. This will ensure that for every month and year, you report on one forecast value per product, and it will help you align with your sales data in a later join.

tasks.label: Task 2:
tasks.copy:
1. Select the Unpivot tile to open its configuration options. 
  2. Under step 1, name the first column "Forecast Product."
  3. Name the next column "Forecast Amount."
  4. Select the columns to collapse: Handheld, Monitor, Keyboard, and Printer.
  5. Use Step 4 to rename the columns if needed. By default the same name of the column will be entered. In this case, we will keep the default names.
  6. Click Run Preview.
  7. Select the Preview tab to ensure the data looks correct.
  8. Select Done.

tasks.label: Task 3:
tasks.copy:
Because you don't have a forecasted value for every day for each product, you do not have a daily granularity for your products. So, we want to aggregate the data into a monthly granularity.

  1. Under the Dates and Numbers category, drag a Date Operations tile onto the canvas, and connect it to the Unpivot tile.
  2. Name your new column "Year"
  3. In the drop-down under step 2, select "Year of date."
  4. Next, select "Month" as the column that contains the values you want to calculate.
  5. Now click Add Date Operation button.
  6. Type in "Month Number."
  7. Select "Month of date."
  8. Select "Month" as the column to use.
  9. Click Done.

Doing this will allow you to join on those fields with all of your other DataSets in a later step.

tasks.label: Task 4:
tasks.copy:
Now, we want to create a constant that exists on every row. The idea here is to then put together the year, month, and constant together to create a date value that is the first day of each month.

  1. Now, add a constant that will allow you to create a day by dragging the Add Constants action onto your canvas from the Utility section.
  2. Connect it to the Date Operations tile.
  3. Click name the new column "Day"
  4. Select the new column's type of data dropdown and choose text.
  5. Enter "01" as the constant to fill the new column.
  6. Click Done.

tasks.label: Task 5:
tasks.copy:
Next, you are going to combine your year, month, and day columns into one field:

  1. Drag the Combine Columns action from the Text section to the canvas.
  2. Connect it to the Add Constants.
  3. Name the new column "Date".
  4. Select "Other" from the What character should separate the combined values drop-down.
  5. Then, in the field below put a "/" (forward slash).
  6. Leave Should original columns being combined be removed unchecked.
  7. Select the columns to combine: Year, Month Number, and Day.
  8. Click Run Preview and view the Preview of your new Date column.
  9. Click Done.

This creates a new field with the year, month, and day combined.

tasks.label: Task 6:
tasks.copy:
You are now going to convert the "Date" column from a text to a date type:

  1. Select the Alter Columns action from the Utility category and drag it onto the canvas and connect it to the Combine Columns tile.
  2. Under step 1, choose the column "Date."
  3. Select "Date" as the cast data type for the column.
  4. You may see a message that says "Failed to convert value '2026/2026-02-12/2/01' from type 'String' to type 'Date'."
  5. Click on the settings icon (gear menu) and select Null from the Bad Values dropdown.
  6. Then, open Data Settings and select Custom Format from the Data and time format dropdown.
  7. Now, select '%Y-%m-%d' from the Date format dropdown.
  8. Click Done. Now you have a field that Domo will interpret as an actual date that you can use for the date range and date grain selections in a card.
  9. Name your DataFlow as "Forecast Sales" + your initials at the top of your screen where it says "Add DataFlow Name."
  10. Click Save.

You will continue building this DataFlow in ETL activity 2: Part 2.

fields.title: Magic ETL Activity 2: Part 2
fields.description: You've now reached the final stage of this activity. The goal from this point forward is to bring in your Sales DataSets and finish building out your DataFlow.

tasks.label: Task 1:
tasks.copy:
1. Download the Power User Sales 2026, 2027, and 2028 DataSets from the file repository and upload them into Domo using the File Upload connector.
  2. Bring the three DataSets into the DataFlow as inputs.
  3. Use the Append Rows tile to combine the three DataSets and make sure to include all the columns.
  4. Review the changes. There should be no changes because these are similar data files—everything matches and won’t need to be adjusted.
  5. Click Done.

tasks.label: Task 2:
tasks.copy:
1. Click and drag to highlight and select the Date Operations through the Alter Columns action.
  2. Select Duplicate from the Options Menu.
  3. Drag this duplication next to the Append Rows tile and sever the dotted line connection to the Forecast DataSet.
  4. Connect the Date Operations 1 to your Append Rows.
  5. To modify, select Date Operations 1. Then, click your Year operation.
  6. Change step 3 from "Month" to "Sold Date."
  7. Select the "Month Number" operation.
  8. Change step 3 from "Month" to "Sold Date."
  9. Click Done. Now the rest of your actions are updated.

tasks.label: Task 3:
tasks.copy:
Next you want to do a Filter Row transform to filter out the Promotion sales:

  1. Select a Filter Rows tile and drag it onto the canvas.
  2. Connect the Alter Columns 1 tile to Filter Rows.
  3. Click the Add Filter Rule button.
  4. Select "Promotion" as the column to filter on.
  5. Choose does not equal as the type of comparison.
  6. Select a specific value from the "Compare against a column or a specific value" dropdown.
  7. Then, type in "Yes" to filter out our promotional items that we don’t want included in our sales data.
  8. Click Done.

tasks.label: Task 4:
tasks.copy:
You will now aggregate the data so that you can return a single row for each product by month and year. For example, it will allow you to show only one number for a specific product in January of 2026:

  1. To do this you will use the Group By tile. Drag and drop the Group By tile to the canvas.
  2. Connect the Filter Rows tile to Group By.
  3. Select both Product and Date as columns that identify the grouping. This will ensure we get a monthly value for each product.
  4. Name the new aggregated column "Sales."
  5. Select Sale Amount from the Select a column to aggregate that will fill the new column dropdown.
  6. Select Sum from the Select how to aggregate the column dropdown.
  7. Check your work! Run a preview to make sure everything looks correct.
  8. Once confirmed that each tile ran successfully, click Done.

tasks.label: Task 5:
tasks.copy:
1. Drag a Join Data tile over to the canvas.
  2. Connect your Alter Columns and Group By tiles to Join Data.
  3. Select Group By as the input on the left side of the inner join. This will automatically place Alter Columns on the right side.
  4. Then, click Equality condition and select "Date" for both the left and right columns.
  5. Click Equality condition again.
  6. Select "Product" as the left column and "Forecast Product" as the right column.
  7. To fix any column naming conflicts, click the +sign und Left Table Alterations.
  8. Select Date and then Drop Column from the menu.
  9. Click Done.
  10. Click Save. Now you have your data joined together.

tasks.label: Task 6:
tasks.copy:
Lastly, let's finish this DataFlow by adding an output DataSet.

  1. Under Ultility, drag a Select Columns tile over to the canvas.
  2. Connect the Join Data tile to the Select Columns tile.
  3. Select the following columns to keep: "Date", "Year", "Month Number", 
    "Product", "Forecast Amount", andf "Sales".
  4. Select Done.
  5. Drag an Output Dataset tile onto the canvas and connect Select Columns tile to it.
  6. Name it "Forecast Sales," with your initials.
  7. Now select Run Preview to make sure it works as expected and that the data outcome is what you need.
  8. Select Save and Run from the orange dropdown arrow next to the Save button.

You have now completed your DataFlow. Nice work!

fields.title: Optimizing Your Magic ETL DataFlows
fields.description:
Magic ETL allows you to transform your DataSets and create actionable visualizations.

Once you've created Magic ETL DataFlows, you can use this checklist to ensure your DataFlows run efficiently.
